name: Cameroon

findings.controller: China Unicom do Brasil; Camtel (co-funders); Huawei Marine (builder)
findings.summary: The roughly 6,000 km SAIL submarine cable between Kribi, Cameroon and Fortaleza, Brazil, co-funded by China Unicom's Brazilian subsidiary and Camtel and built by Huawei Marine, completed installation in September 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: ownership is shared between a PRC carrier subsidiary and Cameroon's state telco, and neither source states who operates the system. Builder Huawei Marine is PRC-origin (now HMN Tech). The audit court (via EcoMatin) reports SAIL entered service, cost 99.66 billion FCFA and was 0.31% utilised at end-2021; coded tier 4 not 5 because use is negligible, not at scale. Cost not converted.

findings.controller: Huawei Technologies (contractor); Export-Import Bank of China (lender)
findings.summary: A presidential decree authorised Cameroon to sign a 198.9 billion FCFA preferential Eximbank of China loan for phase two of the national broadband network, adding 3,000 km of fibre to 13 towns, with Huawei carrying out construction.
findings.analyst_inference: Source confirms only the signing decree, not signature, disbursement or completion; tier 3 reflects a named contractor and lender. Loan value in FCFA not converted. The Zamengoe data centre (CMR-003) is reported as part of the same NBN II programme.

findings.summary: Camtel's Zamengoe Tier III-design data centre near Yaoundé (3,000 m2) was built by a Chinese consortium including China Shenyang International Cooperation and equipped by Huawei under an Exim Bank of China loan; reported value $15 million.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic because state-owned Camtel controls the facility; equipment is Huawei and financing PRC state debt, so the stack inside is PRC-dependent (see CMR-004 on Huawei holding Camtel system access). Coded tier 4: built and equipped, but the source does not confirm operation at scale. Audit 2026-10-22: Huawei equipped it but did not lead the consortium. Pole set prc under the v0.2 equipment rule (Huawei equipment; CMR-004 documents Huawei holding Camtel system access).

findings.summary: Cameroon's audit court found Huawei has supplied and maintained Camtel's IT systems since 2011 with no written agreement, directly managing equipment and holding access codes, and urged a new contract returning full control to Camtel.
findings.analyst_inference: Single secondary report of a public audit (period 2015-2021); the underlying Chambre des comptes report was not located. The same report says about 90% of Camtel's 412.1 billion FCFA bank debt is owed to Eximbank of China. This is direct evidence of PRC operational control, not just supply.

findings.local_actor: Délégation générale à la sûreté nationale (DGSN)
findings.summary: Huawei won a 2017 national police video-surveillance contract after a pilot; by August 2019 a Yaoundé command centre linked about 2,000 Huawei-installed cameras across eight cities, with a second phase of 5,000 more planned.
findings.analyst_inference: Two independent S3 sources but no S1/S2, so not corroborated under the rule. Contract value and financing undisclosed. Status of the 5,000-camera second phase unknown.

findings.summary: US firm Cybastion presented a planned $75 million AI data centre in Douala, paired with a dedicated power plant, at the first US-Cameroon economic dialogue in August 2026; site, capacity, schedule and financing undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Business in Cameroon calls it an investment proposal, not secured financing; no MoU or contract reported, so tier 1.

findings.summary: Cybastion's Douala AI data-centre proposal includes a power plant to supply the facility dedicated capacity; output capacity was not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: The $75 million figure covers the combined project; no split between data centre and power plant reported, so value recorded only on CMR-006.

findings.summary: During a ministerial visit, the government signalled it would work with Douala-based ST Digital to implement the national AI strategy and host national data in the firm's sovereign cloud and Tier 3 data centre; no contract reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic rests on the article calling ST Digital a local firm; ownership and equipment suppliers are not stated.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases, deployments or licence decisions surfaced in data-centre and AI searches

models.null_reason: one targeted search found the national AI strategy and conferences but no frontier-model partnership or sovereign model

corrections.note: Migrated to spec v0.2 (scale, reversal_reason, still_current, builder/financier, base model, opened flags; corroboration recomputed on opened sources) and audit corrections applied.

Was the NBN II Eximbank loan signed and disbursed, and is phase II complete?
Is the Zamengoe data centre operational at scale and who are its tenants?
Status and financing of the 5,000-camera second phase of the DGSN video-surveillance system.
Ownership of ST Digital and any formal agreement under the national AI strategy.
No reversals found in one targeted search; a broader check is warranted.
